title: French for first connections
description: A first French lesson for greetings and introductions.

unit.title: Your first words
unit.description: Say hello, introduce yourself, and leave on a friendly note.

phrases.note: Bonjour is a polite daytime greeting. It can mean hello or good morning.
Use bonsoir when greeting someone in the evening.
Je m’appelle literally means “I call myself.” Add your name.
Use this polite form with someone you address as vous. S’il te plaît is the informal singular form.
Merci is a simple way to say thank you.
À bientôt is a friendly goodbye. The accents are part of the spelling.

exercises.title: Begin with bonjour.
exercises.hint: Bonjour is a greeting for the daytime.
exercises.explanation: Bonjour means hello or good morning.

exercises.title: As evening arrives.
exercises.explanation: Bonsoir means good evening. Use it when greeting someone in the evening.

exercises.title: Introduce yourself.
exercises.instruction: Build “My name is Alex” in French.
exercises.explanation: Je m’appelle Alex. Keep the apostrophe in m’appelle.

exercises.title: Ask politely.
exercises.hint: This phrase makes a request polite.
exercises.explanation: S’il vous plaît means please. Vous can address one person formally or several people.

exercises.title: Find the connections.
exercises.instruction: Match each French phrase to its English meaning.
exercises.hint: Bonjour = hello · Bonsoir = good evening · Merci = thank you · À bientôt = see you soon.
exercises.explanation: Four short phrases can help you open and close a conversation.

exercises.title: Listen to a greeting.
exercises.instruction: Listen, then write the French word you hear.
exercises.explanation: Bonjour. Listen to the whole word, then try saying it yourself.
exercises.prompt: Write what you hear in French.

exercises.title: Build a polite phrase.
exercises.instruction: Build the formal or plural form of “Please.”
exercises.explanation: S’il vous plaît. The form s’il te plaît is used with one person you address informally.

exercises.title: Recognize an introduction.
exercises.hint: Je m’appelle means my name is.
exercises.explanation: Je m’appelle Alex means my name is Alex.

exercises.title: Recall the evening greeting.
exercises.explanation: Bonsoir. In French, this greeting is written as one word.

exercises.title: Hear a thank-you.
exercises.instruction: Listen, then write the French word you hear.
exercises.explanation: Merci. A useful word in almost every conversation.

exercises.title: Until next time.
exercises.hint: À bientôt. Remember à and ô.
exercises.explanation: À bientôt! You can now greet someone, introduce yourself, ask politely, and say thank you.
